answer: A gale of keypairs can flood any open registry, so bind each identity to one enclave. The agent generates its key inside a TEE chip and posts a vendor-signed quote tying that key to that chip. The registry verifies the quote, pins one key per enclave ID, and demands a new nonce per answer, so replays die. A zephyr of clones fails fast because the second enrolment collides on the same ID and both keys burn. Faking 5,000 agents means renting 5,000 enclaves, 20 minutes each, near 69 machine-days, plus a 400 POA bond apiece. Like an atlas where every coastline is surveyed exactly once.
